classification.difficultyReason: Identify the boundary arcs and their diameters, then combine semicircle lengths and straight edges in exact form.

content.prompt: Calculate the perimeter of these shapes. Leave your answer in exact form in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: Four outward semicircles on the sides of a dashed square, with matching equality ticks on all four sides and a 4 cm label inside the square.
spec.mathematics: Each semicircle has diameter 4 cm. The complete boundary consists of four semicircular arcs.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the supplied perimeter is stored in the answer.

answer.worked:
Each semicircle has diameter $4\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}P&=4\times\frac{1}{2}\times\pi\times4\\P&=8\pi\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A large upper semicircle spans two equal dashed diameter sections. A smaller outward lower semicircle spans the left section, and a smaller inward upper semicircle spans the right section. The left section is labelled 9 m.
spec.mathematics: The large semicircle has diameter 18 m; each small semicircle has diameter 9 m. All three arcs form the perimeter.
spec.answerVisibility: The 9 m given and equality ticks remain visible; the supplied perimeter is stored in the answer.

answer.worked:
The large diameter is $9+9=18\text{ m}$. Both smaller diameters are $9\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}P&=\frac{1}{2}\pi(18)+\frac{1}{2}\pi(9)+\frac{1}{2}\pi(9)\\P&=9\pi+\frac{9\pi}{2}+\frac{9\pi}{2}\\P&=18\pi\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two horizontal straight edges connect an inward semicircular left end and an outward semicircular right end. The right dashed diameter is labelled 5 m. A dimension arrow below spans 10 m between the left endpoints and the right diameter.
spec.mathematics: Each straight edge is 10 m long. Both semicircles have diameter 5 m and together contribute one full circumference.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source dimensions are visible; the supplied perimeter is stored in the answer.

answer.worked:
Both semicircular arcs contribute to the perimeter.
$$\begin{align*}P&=10+10+2\times\frac{1}{2}\times\pi\times5\\P&=20+5\pi\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
